subject: Re: N-Grammer kickoff — repro done, FLOP study early read
body:
Hi both,

Status:

- Reproduction milestone met (late by a week — C4 queue times on titan, not model issues). N-Grammer beats our Transformer baseline on C4 perplexity at matched parameter count and edges the Primer config we run internally; SuperGLUE classification shows the same ordering. The release's claims hold up in our stack.
- FLOP study early read: at matched quality, the n-gram-augmented config needs roughly 0.85x the training FLOPs of the baseline, and the latent n-gram lookup adds under 2% inference overhead. The interesting knob is the discrete latent vocab size — too small and the n-grams stop helping, too large and embedding memory becomes the cost. We're mapping that curve now; it will be the centerpiece of the June readout.
- Risk: SuperGLUE fine-tuning variance is high on small tasks, so I'm running 5 seeds before quoting deltas. Might push the FLOP report to 07-03.

Rafael's API work spins up next week per plan.

Gustavo
